main_issue: Whether strong-smelling food (D's fish curry) can be cooked in the shared kitchen, and what rule applies given A's weekday-before-7pm request versus B and C's any-time objection.

A-B.evidence: B backs A's ban at turn 2, but by turns 22-25 B rejects A's narrow before-7pm proposal as 'not a separate issue'; A insists it is separate (24).

A-C.evidence: C agreed at turn 3, but at turns 9, 15 and 23 C says timing doesn't matter, which conflicts with A's time-limited proposal; C never directly rejects A.

A-D.evidence: D resists the ban (4, 10, 16); A narrows the ask to weekdays before 7 pm (11, 17), which D still questions (18).

B-C.evidence: Both say timing is irrelevant and the smell affects them anyway (8-9, 14-15, 22-23); C backs B ('She's right').

B-D.evidence: B began by supporting a ban on D's cooking (2), but later argues for one rule for all (25) and rejects A's special treatment. D cites B and C against A (12, 18). The two never settle on a shared arrangement.

C-D.evidence: C complained about the curry smell on laundry (3). D uses C's 'time doesn't matter' point against A (12), and C backs B's stance (23), which is not a direct agreement with D.
